topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series, introduces its audience and sets out the learning outcomes for this lecture.

topics.label: Accumulating gene changes in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the stepwise accumulation of gene changes as a model of cancer development and identifies the questions that model raises.

topics.label: Cancer as disrupted differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer through the loss of normal tissue organization and show why studying isolated cells cannot fully capture that disruption.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumors through invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how invasion and metastatic spread distinguish malignant tumors from contained benign growths, using clinical and histological examples.

topics.label: Tumor progression and the risks of benign tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what benign status implies about a tumor's future behavior, using colorectal progression and exceptions to show that neither progression nor harmlessness is guaranteed.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor names encode tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor growth compromises normal bodily function and produces potentially fatal disease.

topics.label: Patterns of tumor incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the frequency and distribution of tumor types across populations and species.

topics.label: Cancer detection and screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the rationale for detecting tumors early and assess how effectively screening achieves that goal in different cancers.

topics.label: Lecture close and follow-up
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by returning to the learning outcomes and directing students toward revision and upcoming teaching.
